findings.evidence: Symmetry.lean:192,208 list `hτ, ← indexEquiv_neg g, indexNeg_neg` together; EquivInvariance.lean:82 states `indexEquiv_neg` with RHS `-g.indexEquiv i`, which `indexNeg_neg` itself rewrites, so the `@[simp]` RHS is not simp-normal either.
findings.fix: Restate the transport lemma without `Neg`/`letI` as `indexEquiv_reflectionPerm_self : g.indexEquiv (P.reflectionPerm i i) = P₂.reflectionPerm (g.indexEquiv i) (g.indexEquiv i)` and use it (as `←`) alongside `indexNeg_neg`; the two then act on disjoint redexes and the rewrite is confluent.
findings.issue: The `simp only` set contains both `indexNeg_neg` (`-i = P.reflectionPerm i i`, generated `@[simp]` by `@[simps]` on `RootPairing.indexNeg`, Defs.lean:403) and `← indexEquiv_neg g` (`-(g.indexEquiv i) = g.indexEquiv (P.reflectionPerm i i)`). After `hτ` rewrites `↑(τ i)` to `g.indexEquiv i`, both rules match the redex `-(g.indexEquiv i)` and produce different results; only one order leaves the goal in a shape `Equiv.apply_eq_iff_eq` can close, so the proof depends on simp's internal rule ordering, not on anything visible. Same in `submatrix_geckIndexEquiv_f` (line 208). Mathlib's own proofs about `e`/`f`/`ω` explicitly disable this lemma (`simp [e, h, -indexNeg_neg]`, GeckConstruction/Basic.lean:356; `simp [ω, -indexNeg_neg]`, :248).

findings.evidence: `Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/RootSystem/Chain.lean:266` `chainTopCoeff_reflectionPerm_left : P.chainTopCoeff (P.reflectionPerm i i) j = P.chainBotCoeff i j` and `:277` `chainBotCoeff_reflectionPerm_left`, both `@[simp]`, under `variable {ι R M N} [Finite ι] [CommRing R] [CharZero R] [IsDomain R] ... [P.IsCrystallographic]` (Chain.lean:37-42).
findings.fix: Derive it: `rw [← chainTopCoeff_reflectionPerm_left, ← indexEquiv_reflectionPerm_self, chainTopCoeff_indexEquiv, chainTopCoeff_reflectionPerm_left]` (instance requirements of `Chain.lean` match this file's `Chain` section exactly).
findings.issue: `chainBotCoeff_indexEquiv` repeats `chainTopCoeff_indexEquiv` verbatim (same `by_cases`, same `key`, same `le_antisymm`) with add↔sub and Top↔Bot swapped; the reusable fact that the two coefficients swap under index negation is already in Mathlib and is hidden here.

findings.evidence: EquivInvariance.lean:64-65 vs. its uses at :140 and :159, where the goal is produced by `rw [← map_add]`/`← map_sub` in `range`-membership form.
findings.fix: State it as `g.toHom.weightMap m ∈ range P₂.root ↔ m ∈ range P.root`; the two `exact`s then match syntactically and the `@[simp]` form is uniform.
findings.issue: `mem_range_root_weightMap_iff` is stated with the left side unfolded (`∃ i, P₂.root i = g.toHom.weightMap m`) while the right side uses `∈ range`; the two uses (`exact mem_range_root_weightMap_iff g` at lines 140 and 159) then close a goal of the form `_ ∈ range P₂.root ↔ _ ∈ range P.root` only through the definitional unfolding of `Set.range` membership.

summary: Two proof-quality issues: the negation-transport lemma is stated against `Neg` so that the `simp only` sets in `submatrix_geckIndexEquiv_e`/`_f` contain two rules (`indexNeg_neg` and `← indexEquiv_neg`) that match the same redex and rewrite it incompatibly, and `chainBotCoeff_indexEquiv` duplicates the whole 14-line `chainTopCoeff_indexEquiv` proof instead of deriving it in four rewrites from Mathlib's `chain*Coeff_reflectionPerm_left`.
